chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him about the Sa'i (running) between al-Safa and al-Marwah. He said: 'When you reach the house on your right at the beginning of the valley, perform Sa'i until you reach the first alley on your right after crossing the valley towards al-Marwah. When you reach it, stop the Sa'i and walk. And when you come from al-Marwah, start from the alley I described to you. When you reach the door facing al-Safa after crossing the valley, stop the Sa'i and walk. Indeed, the Sa'i is obligatory for men, and there is no Sa'i for women.'

key_terms.اَلسَّعْيُ: Sa'i: The ritual walking or running between Safa and Marwah
key_terms.اَلصَّفَا: Al-Safa: One of the two hills between which Sa'i is performed
key_terms.اَلْمَرْوَةُ: Al-Marwah: The second of the two hills between which Sa'i is performed
key_terms.اَلْوَادِي: Al-Wadi: The valley or low ground, often referring to the area between the hills in Mecca

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between men and women in performing Sa'i between Safa and Marwah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* provides a precise geographical delineation of the Sa'i route, specifying that the ritual running (ramal) is confined to the section between the first valley and the first alleyway on the right. It highlights a key juristic distinction in Shia fiqh where men are obligated to perform the hastened running, whereas women are exempt and simply walk, reflecting the principle of easing religious obligations for women.
